newsitem.title: USA: Texas power prices move higher with cold weather.
newsitem.headline: Texas power prices move higher with cold weather.

text.p: Wholesale electricity prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) moved higher Monday after colder weather took over and pushed temperatures below some expectations, industry sources said.
"With the cooler temperatures there is not so many utilities selling," said one ERCOT power broker.
Temperatures through much of Texas were expected to reach only the 40s and 50s degrees Fahrenheit area today, and were forecast to remain below normal through to December 3.
A winter storm swept through parts of Texas over the weekend, bringing snow and icy roads to regions that had been expected to experience rain.
ERCOT firm, peak power for Tuesday delivery was assessed in the $31.50-32.50 range after unconfirmed morning trades at $31.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), the brokers and marketers said.
ERCOT peak power had been trading at $29.00-31.00 late last week.
Off-peak non-firm ERCOT power transactions were pegged at $17.00-18.00 for Tuesday delivery from $10.00-12.00 late last week, the sources said.
ERCOT December peak power bids were said to have moved lower, putting talk in the $31.00-33.00 range from discussion at $33.00-33.75 last week.
January/February peak power was steady at $31.50-32.00, the sources said.
